subject: Push new builds to git_hub download automagically?

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Push new builds to git_hub download automagically?
parts:
It is so helpful to be able to just say 
devtools::document("~/bin/umx"); devtools::install("~/bin/umx"); devtools::build("~/bin/umx")

Is it possible to tell build() to push the file to github, replacing the file of the same name in the most recent download?

This would mean that a call to install_github("tbates/umx") always pulled what the developer had last built, without the developer needing to go to github pages and point and click and drag and drop (even though this rocks, it gets a bit tedious if you are fixing/pushing things a couple of times a day

thanks again for a cool tool!

t

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Re: Push new builds to git_hub download automagically?
parts:
Hi Winston,
All the package files are fine and going via the git interface. It's just the .files that devtools::build() outputs - i.e., packagName_0.5.tar.gz that need to be set as downloadables from the master, no?

Surely it's not the case that install_github() pulls all the files from master rather than grabbing the build?

On Wednesday, November 20, 2013 4:07:08 PM UTC, Winston Chang wrote:
Hi - what files are you dragging and dropping? With the usual git workflow, you shouldn't need to use GitHub's web interface at all - just add files, commit, and push. This can be done from the command line, or from various graphical tools.

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Push new builds to git_hub download automagically?
parts: On Wed, Nov 20, 2013 at 10:24 AM, Timothy Bates <timothy...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Winston,
All the package files are fine and going via the git interface. It's just the .files that devtools::build() outputs - i.e., packagName_0.5.tar.gz that need to be set as downloadables from the master, no?

Surely it's not the case that install_github() pulls all the files from master rather than grabbing the build?

It is the case -- install_github grabs the zip file which contains all the files from master (or other branch/tag, if specified). It's the same as if you click the "Download ZIP" button on the project page. The zip file is automatically generated by Github. Then it's built and installed on the user's machine.

-Winston

> you click the "Download ZIP" button on the project page. The zip file is
> automatically generated by Github. Then it's built and installed on the
> user's machine.

I think Timothy's interested in distributing binary builds via github.
This is certainly possible to do (and would be relatively easy to
automate in devtools), but I don't think it's the right approach.
It's not clear exactly what the right approach is yet, but I suspect
it involves checking and building on https://travis-ci.org/, then
uploading the binary artifact to a hosting service (probably s3), then
either constructing the appropriate url, or using a webserver to
provide an overlay that mimics the usual R repo structure.

Hadley

> It is the case -- install_github grabs the zip file which contains all the files from master (or other branch/tag, if specified). It's the same as if you click the "Download ZIP" button on the project page. The zip file is automatically generated by Github

Wow. OK. I thought I had to manually put the output of build() into the downloads section.

Just tried this now, and it works as you say: the master.zip is downloaded... Cool!

Re Hadley's question: I would like to deploy binaries, but that wasn't my question here. I just didn't realise that one needs do nothing as a devleoper for install_github to deliver the up to date build !-)

I am a bit baffled as to why R doesn't have OS-independent packages... Some format which, like docx, works on all platforms.

I could understand for  packages with compiled fortran etc. but then you'd think a fat-package would work with a platform folder inside compiled: containing the compiled code for each platform.

But for packages that are just a zipped folder of R and Rd files, I'd have thought was automatically cross platform. But that's another issue and mostly my ignorance, I am sure.

Thanks for the help winston! and hadley!

t

> then

https://gist.github.com/jefferis/7572583

Not sure if this idea could be of any general use. Comments welcome.
